reason: H0 exclusively configures and exercises the JSON decoder, while S1 changes CRC64 ECMA hashing and introduces a CPU-selected x86 SSE4.2 implementation. Consequently, H0 cannot reach the new CRC64 entry points or test their stateful and boundary-sensitive behavior.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON but no CRC64 module.
H0 calls wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson; it never constructs or invokes ecma_hasher.
ecma_hasher.update! selects up_x86_sse42 only when this.state == 0, making initial versus incremental update state material.
ecma_hasher.up_x86_sse42! has alignment handling, a short-input threshold at 0x20, 0x10-byte chunk processing, and tail handling based on length modulo 16.
The accelerated implementation uses x86 SSE4.2 operations and therefore adds a CPU-dependent implementation path absent from H0.
recommended_action: Add a CRC64 ECMA fuzz harness that exercises update!, update_u64!, and checksum_u64 across one-shot and variably chunked updates, varied input alignment, and lengths around 0x10 and 0x20 boundaries; compare accelerated results against the generic up! implementation and verify identical final checksums.
